title: Microsoft Dataverse: run prompt columns on existing records in bulk (backfill)
summary: Hold: the AI prompts switch has a documented Dataverse automation setting, contrary to the table's claim that automation is undocumented. The notes also mistake the bulk checkbox for the action that queues a job, and the cost rationale incorrectly implies that every execution consumes both credit currencies.

claims.where: What's changing; rationale: risk

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: third table row
claims.claim: An automation operation for the AI prompts environment switch is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /organizations(organizationid) ... AiPromptsEnabled ... Indicates whether AI Prompts feature is enabled. ... LogicalName ... aipromptsenabled
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api to kind 'rest', call 'PATCH /organizations(<organizationid>)', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/organization'. Add to its note: 'The request body sets aipromptsenabled, a Boolean that enables or disables AI prompts.' The v9.2 Web API reference also documents this property at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/organization?view=dataverse-latest.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Backfill generates values asynchronously in a background System jobs job rather than asking for approval of each generated record.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout

claims.where: What's changing: historical execution behaviour
claims.claim: The existing execution mechanism runs on record creation or a change to an input column, rather than automatically populating pre-existing records when the column is added.
claims.quote: Prompt column values are populated when records are created and when the input column values are updated. When prompt columns are added to tables with records, the existing records' new prompt columns aren't populated automatically.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/specialized-columns#prompt-columns for the historical execution behaviour; that supporting page is absent from sources.

claims.where: What's changing: FAQ statement
claims.claim: The FAQ says changing a prompt definition does not recalculate existing values until a later input-column update.
claims.quote: updating the prompt definition does not recalculate existing prompt values until a subsequent update occurs on one or more columns defined in the prompt.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn documents backfill as rolling out and potentially unavailable in the reader's region, in contrast to the roadmap's In development status.
claims.quote: Apply prompt to existing records in bulk ... This capability is in process of rolling out, and might not be available in your region yet.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: Capacity; Governance guidance: Before rollout

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Prompt columns provide input-column data to an AI model to generate responses, including historical records selected for backfill.
claims.quote: The AI model processes these prompts to generate relevant responses based on specified input columns. ... Use this option to run the prompt for existing records in bulk (backfill).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Generated prompt values persist in a column in the source table and can be used by apps reading that table.
claims.quote: The result is immediately stored in the prompt column, ready to be used in apps, workflows, or reports. ... The key function is that the prompt column contains generative AI results stored in the table persistently.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Access to the generated prompt column governs who can see its output, so its column security needs checking.
claims.quote: When a calculated column or prompt column includes a column that is secured, data might be displayed in the calculated or prompt column to users that don't have permission to the secured column. Both the original column and the calculated or prompt column should be secured.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/field-level-security for the prompt-column visibility and security advice; the existing sources do not state this access-control premise.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure

claims.where: rationale: cost

claims.fix: Replace the cost rationale with 'Variable. Prompt columns consume credits each time a prompt executes; the activity report shows whether an execution used AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits, so a bulk backfill can consume substantial credits.'

claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullets beginning 'Check the available AI credit capacity', 'Monitor jobs in System jobs' and 'Review the Estimated consumption column'. Keep the existing capacity and monitoring information in the body; these checklist controls lack table rows.
